name: gn_h3_scale_geometry_diag_v1
perturbation: Identical previous rule: delta=-epsilon0*scale*sign(u.T@g_new_gradient)*u, eta_k=epsilon/abs(z_new); no optimizer updates.
primary_predictor: g_old_probe.T@delta; exact same held-out windows as measured NLL, derivative calibration only

fisher.approximation: 8 frozen independent model action samples per old_build window; 128 windows; no gradient through sampled actions
fisher.action_metric: full official GMM log density; no Wa rescaling, label replacement or empirical expert-score approximation
fisher.interpretation: Model Fisher MC estimate, NOT claimed equal to expert NLL Hessian or exact GGN; includes mixture means, weights and scales

rules.good_scale: 16 numerically evaluable directions, conservative sign accuracy >=.9375 (15/16), Spearman>=.9, Pearson>=.9
rules.local_recovery: smallest scale good, sign accuracy improves >=.125, relative linearization error drops >=4x
rules.material_geometry_advantage: at least two pre-fixed scales improve accuracy >=.125 and Spearman >=.15, without lower evaluable coverage
rules.limits: Descriptive engineering criteria; not statistical significance. If both smallest-scale calibrations fail: unresolved Taylor regime/measurement, NOT evidence that gradient directional derivatives are invalid.

limitations: Fisher Monte Carlo approximation is one fixed draw set, not repeated reference estimation.
The two eigenspaces change direction identity and functional displacement at equal parameter norm; this comparison cannot uniquely prove previous functional definition was wrong.
Same-probe Taylor agreement is not cross-trajectory relation generalization.
No control, optimizer or rollout benefit tested.
